claims.explanation: Dofetilide is a potent blocker of the hERG/KCNH2 potassium channel, and its selective anticancer activity likely reflects dependence on KCNH2 (or related potassium channels) for proliferation/survival in certain lineages. Lines with high KCNH2 expression or mutations that drive potassium-channel-dependent growth (e.g., EGFR, KRAS, BRAF, PTEN loss) are sensitized, while lines with low KCNH2 expression or alternative survival pathways are protected.

features.basis: Dofetilide is a high-affinity hERG/KCNH2 blocker; expression of the target is required for drug effect
EGFR-mutant lines (HCC4006, NCIH1793, KNS81) are among the most killed; EGFR signaling can regulate potassium channels and survival
KRAS-mutant lines (NCIH441, ASPC1, QGP1, T3M4) are enriched among sensitive lines, possibly via MAPK-driven K+ channel dependence
BRAF-mutant lines (UACC62, MFE319, SNUC5) appear among sensitive lines, suggesting MAPK pathway addiction may increase K+ channel dependence
PTEN loss (UACC62, SNU466, ZR751, H4, MFE319) is common in sensitive lines; PI3K/AKT activation may upregulate K+ channels
TP53 mutations are frequent in sensitive lines, though also in resistant lines, so this is weak evidence
ARID1A mutations appear in several sensitive lines (EFE184, NCIH1793, MFE319, SNUC5), but also in resistant lines, so weak
Dofetilide also targets KCNH1 (Eag1), which is overexpressed in many cancers and promotes proliferation
Dofetilide targets KCNJ12 (Kir2.2); expression may contribute to sensitivity in some lines
Dofetilide targets KCNK2 (TREK-1); expression could mediate effects in lines lacking KCNH2
STK11 mutations appear in resistant lines (EKVX, NCIH1623) and one sensitive line, suggesting possible protection
KEAP1 mutations appear in resistant lines (NCIH1623, HEC265), possibly via NRF2-mediated survival
